p.src: Now Dong Zhuo, whose courtesy name was Zhongying, was a native of Lintao in Longxi. He had been appointed Governor of Hedong and had always been arrogant. That day he treated Xuande with contempt, and Zhang Fei, his temper flaring, was ready to kill him. Xuande and Lord Guan hastily restrained him, saying, “He is an official appointed by the court. How can you kill him on your own authority?” Zhang Fei said, “If we do not kill that scoundrel, yet must take orders under him, I cannot bear it! If you two elder brothers wish to remain here, do so; I shall go elsewhere by myself!” Xuande said, “We three are bound by honor to share life and death. How could we part? We had better all go elsewhere.” Zhang Fei said, “If so, my resentment will be somewhat eased.” Thereupon the three led their troops through the night to join Zhu Jun. Zhu Jun treated them generously, combined their forces with his own, and advanced against Zhang Bao. At this time Cao Cao was accompanying Huangfu Song in the campaign against Zhang Liang, and they fought a great battle at Quyang. Meanwhile, Zhu Jun advanced against Zhang Bao. Zhang Bao led eighty or ninety thousand rebels and encamped behind the mountain. Zhu Jun appointed Xuande his vanguard and sent him against the rebels. Zhang Bao sent his lieutenant Gao Sheng forth on horseback to issue a challenge. Xuande sent Zhang Fei to meet him. Zhang Fei spurred his horse and leveled his spear. After only a few exchanges with Gao Sheng, he thrust him from the saddle. Xuande waved his troops forward in a direct charge. Zhang Bao, still mounted, loosened his hair, brandished his sword, and began to work sorcery. At once wind and thunder raged, and a mass of black vapor descended from the sky; within it seemed to be countless soldiers and horses charging to attack. Xuande hurriedly recalled his troops. His army fell into chaos and returned defeated, whereupon he conferred with Zhu Jun. Zhu Jun said, “He employs sorcery. Tomorrow we can slaughter pigs, sheep, and dogs, collect their blood, and have soldiers lie in ambush on the mountaintop. When the rebels pursue us, let the soldiers pour it down from the high slope; that will break the spell.”

p.src: Xuande obeyed. He assigned Lord Guan and Zhang Fei a thousand soldiers each to lie in ambush on high ridges behind the mountain, prepared with vessels of pigs’, sheep’s, and dogs’ blood and other filth. The next day Zhang Bao, with banners waving and drums beating, led his troops forth to challenge, and Xuande went out to meet him. As battle was joined, Zhang Bao worked his magic. Wind and thunder raged, sand flew and stones hurtled, black vapor covered the sky, and surging ranks of men and horses descended from the heavens. Xuande wheeled his horse and fled, and Zhang Bao drove his troops in pursuit. Just as they were passing the mountaintop, Guan and Zhang’s ambushers fired the signal cannon and poured down all the filth together. Then paper soldiers and straw horses were seen tumbling from the sky; the wind and thunder instantly ceased, and the sand and stones flew no more. Seeing that his spell had been broken, Zhang Bao hastened to withdraw his army. Lord Guan’s troops came out on the left and Zhang Fei’s on the right, while Xuande and Zhu Jun pressed forward together from the rear. The rebel army was utterly defeated. Xuande caught sight of the banner of the General of the Earth and galloped after it, but Zhang Bao fled in panic. Xuande loosed an arrow and struck him in the left arm. Zhang Bao escaped with the arrow still in him, fled into Yangcheng, and held fast without coming out. Zhu Jun led his troops in surrounding and attacking Yangcheng, while also sending men to learn news of Huangfu Song. The scout returned and reported in detail: “Huangfu Song has won a great victory. Because Dong Zhuo suffered repeated defeats, the court ordered Huangfu Song to replace him. By the time Huangfu Song arrived, Zhang Jue was already dead. Zhang Liang took command of his followers and opposed our army, but Huangfu Song defeated him in seven successive battles and slew him at Quyang. They opened Zhang Jue’s coffin, mutilated the corpse, displayed his severed head, and sent it to the capital. All the remaining rebels surrendered. The court promoted Huangfu Song to General of Chariots and Cavalry and appointed him Governor of Ji Province. Huangfu Song also memorialized that Lu Zhi had rendered meritorious service and committed no crime, so the court restored Lu Zhi to his former office. Cao Cao likewise received an appointment as Chancellor of Jinan for his achievements, and is to disband his troops and assume office without delay.” On hearing this, Zhu Jun urged on his troops and attacked Yangcheng with all his strength. The rebels’ position became desperate, and their officer Yan Zheng stabbed Zhang Bao to death, presented his head, and surrendered. Zhu Jun then pacified several commanderies and submitted a memorial announcing his victory.

p.src: At this time three remnants of the Yellow Turbans—Zhao Hong, Han Zhong, and Sun Zhong—gathered tens of thousands of followers, burning and plundering wherever they went and declaring that they would avenge Zhang Jue. The court ordered Zhu Jun to lead his victorious army against them at once. Obeying the edict, Zhu Jun led his army forward. The rebels then occupied Wancheng. Zhu Jun led his troops against it, and Zhao Hong sent Han Zhong out to fight. Zhu Jun sent Xuande, Guan, and Zhang to attack the southwestern corner of the city. Han Zhong brought all his elite troops to the southwestern corner to resist them. Zhu Jun himself unleashed two thousand armored cavalry and headed straight for the northeastern corner. Fearing that the city would be lost, the rebels hastily abandoned the southwest and turned back. Xuande fell upon them from behind. The rebels were heavily defeated and fled into Wancheng. Zhu Jun divided his forces and sealed off the city on all four sides. When provisions ran out within, Han Zhong sent a man out to offer surrender. Zhu Jun refused. Xuande said, “In former times, Gaozu won the empire chiefly because he could summon surrender and receive those who submitted. Why, sir, do you reject Han Zhong?” Zhu Jun replied, “That was one time; this is another. During the conflict between Qin and Xiang, the empire was in chaos and the people had no settled ruler. Therefore surrender was invited and allegiance rewarded, to encourage others to come over. Now all within the seas is united, and only the Yellow Turbans have rebelled. If we permit them to surrender, there will be no means of encouraging good conduct. It would let rebels plunder at will when they have the advantage and surrender whenever they lose. That would embolden brigands and is no sound policy.” Xuande said, “It is right not to accept the rebels’ surrender. But now they are hemmed in on all sides as if within an iron barrel. If their plea to surrender is denied, they will surely fight to the death. Even ten thousand men united in purpose cannot be withstood; how much less the tens of thousands within the city who are resolved to die? It would be better to withdraw from the east and south and attack only from the west and north. The rebels will surely abandon the city and flee. With no heart left for battle, they can then be captured at once.” Zhu Jun agreed. He withdrew the troops from the eastern and southern sides and ordered a concerted attack from the west and north. As expected, Han Zhong led his troops out of the city and fled. Zhu Jun, Xuande, Guan, and Zhang led their three armies in a sudden pursuit, shot Han Zhong dead, and scattered all the rest in flight.

p.src: While the pursuit was under way, Zhao Hong and Sun Zhong arrived with the rebel host and engaged Zhu Jun in battle. Seeing the strength of Zhao Hong’s forces, Zhu Jun temporarily withdrew his army. Taking advantage of the moment, Zhao Hong recaptured Wancheng. Zhu Jun encamped ten li away. Just as he was preparing to attack, he suddenly saw a body of troops approaching from due east. The general at their head had a broad brow and wide face, with the mighty frame of a tiger and the stout waist of a bear. He was a native of Fuchun in Wu Commandery. His surname was Sun, his given name Jian, and his courtesy name Wentai; he was a descendant of Sun Wuzi. At the age of seventeen, while traveling with his father to Qiantang, he saw more than ten pirates who had robbed merchants of their goods and were dividing the spoils on the bank. Sun Jian said to his father, “These bandits can be captured.” Exerting all his strength, he took up his sword and went ashore, shouting loudly and gesturing east and west as though summoning men. Believing that government troops had arrived, the pirates abandoned all the goods and fled. Sun Jian overtook them and killed one of the pirates. Through this feat his name became known throughout the commandery and counties, and he was recommended for appointment as a commandant. Later, the sorcerous rebel Xu Chang of Kuaiji rose in revolt, proclaimed himself Emperor Yangming, and gathered tens of thousands of followers. Sun Jian and the commandery’s military officer recruited more than a thousand brave men, joined forces with the provincial and commandery troops, defeated the rebels, and slew Xu Chang and his son Xu Shao. Inspector Zang Min memorialized his achievements. Sun Jian was appointed Assistant Magistrate of Yandu, and later Assistant Magistrate of Xuyi and then Xiapi. Now, seeing the Yellow Turban rebels arise, he had gathered young men from his home district, traveling merchants, and more than fifteen hundred elite troops from the Huai and Si regions, and had come to lend support.

Sun Zhong led the rebels in a breakout through the north gate and came face-to-face with Xuande. With no heart to fight, he sought only to escape. Xuande drew his bow and loosed an arrow. Throughout the Nanyang region, more than ten commanderies were pacified. Zhu Jun returned triumphantly to the capital and by imperial decree was appointed General of Chariots and Cavalry and Intendant of Henan. Zhu Jun submitted a memorial reporting the merits of Sun Jian, Liu Bei, and the others. Sun Jian had influential connections and was appointed assistant military officer in another commandery, whereupon he departed to take office; only Xuande waited for a long time without receiving any appointment.

p.src: The three men, gloomy and dispirited, were strolling through the streets when the carriage of Court Gentleman Zhang Jun happened to pass. Xuande approached him and recounted his achievements. Zhang Jun was greatly shocked. He entered the court and addressed the Emperor: “When the Yellow Turbans rebelled, the root cause was that the Ten Attendants sold offices and titles. They employed none but their favorites and executed none but their enemies, thereby plunging the realm into chaos. The Ten Attendants should now be beheaded, their heads displayed in the southern suburbs, and envoys sent to proclaim the deed throughout the realm. Let those of merit be richly rewarded, and all within the four seas will naturally return to peace.” The Ten Attendants told the Emperor, “Zhang Jun has deceived his sovereign.” The Emperor ordered his guards to drive Zhang Jun out. The Ten Attendants conferred together: “These complaints must come from men who earned merit in defeating the Yellow Turbans but received no appointment. For the present, have the appointment office register them for minor posts. It will not be too late to deal with them afterward.” Thus Xuande was appointed county commandant of Anxi County in Zhongshan Prefecture, Dingzhou, and was ordered to take office on a fixed date. Xuande dismissed his troops to their native places. Taking only some twenty personal attendants, he came with Guan and Zhang to assume office in Anxi County. After administering the county for a month, he had not taken so much as a hair from the people, and all were won over by his virtue. After taking office, he shared a table with Guan and Zhang at meals and a bed with them at night. Whenever Xuande sat among a large gathering, Guan and Zhang stood in attendance all day without tiring.

p.src: Before four months had passed since his arrival, the court issued an edict ordering the dismissal of all local officials who had gained office through military merit. Xuande suspected that he was among those to be dismissed. Just then an imperial inspector arrived in the county on his circuit. Xuande went beyond the outer walls to welcome him and saluted him. The inspector remained seated on his horse and merely gestured faintly with his whip in acknowledgment. Guan and Zhang were both enraged. Upon reaching the posthouse, the inspector took the honored seat facing south, while Xuande stood in attendance below the steps. After a long while the inspector asked, “From what background does Commandant Liu come?” Xuande replied, “I, Bei, am a descendant of Prince Jing of Zhongshan. Since joining the campaign against the Yellow Turbans in Zhuo Commandery, I have fought more than thirty battles, great and small, and rendered some slight service. For that reason I received my present office.” The inspector roared, “You falsely claim kinship with the imperial house and make false reports of your achievements! The court's present edict is intended precisely to purge corrupt and unworthy officials such as you!” Murmuring assent again and again, Xuande withdrew. On returning to the county office, he consulted the clerks. One clerk said, “The inspector's show of authority means nothing other than that he wants a bribe.” Xuande said, “I have not taken so much as a hair from the people. Where could I obtain valuables to give him?” The next day, the inspector first summoned the county clerks and coerced them into accusing the commandant of harming the people. Xuande went several times in person to plead for their release, but each time the gate guards barred his way and refused him an audience.

I return this seal and sash and depart from this place forever!” The inspector returned and reported the matter to the Governor of Dingzhou, who forwarded an official dispatch to the provincial authorities and sent men to arrest them. Xuande, Guan, and Zhang went to Daizhou to seek refuge with Liu Hui. When Liu Hui learned that Xuande was a kinsman of the Han imperial house, he concealed him in his home. Zhang Fei said, “What are we waiting for if we do not beat such a villain who preys upon the people to death?”
The inspector pleaded, “Lord Xuande, save my life!”
Xuande was compassionate by nature and hastily shouted at Zhang Fei to stop.
Lord Guan came around from the side and said, “Brother, after rendering so many great services, you received only the post of county commandant, and now this inspector has humiliated you.
In my view, a thicket of thorns is no roost for luan and phoenix;
we would do better to kill the inspector, abandon office, return home, and devise some greater plan.”
Xuande then took his seal and sash, hung them around the inspector's neck, and rebuked him: “For your abuse of the people, you deserve to be killed;
for now, however, I shall spare your life.
I return this seal and sash and depart from this place forever!”
The inspector returned and reported the matter to the Governor of Dingzhou, who forwarded an official dispatch to the provincial authorities and sent men to arrest them.
Xuande, Guan, and Zhang went to Daizhou to seek refuge with Liu Hui.
When Liu Hui learned that Xuande was a kinsman of the Han imperial house, he concealed him in his home. We shall speak no more of this for now.

p.src: Now the Ten Attendants, having seized great power, agreed among themselves that anyone who refused to obey them should be put to death. Zhao Zhong and Zhang Rang sent agents to demand gold and silk from the officers who had defeated the Yellow Turbans; those who refused were denounced and dismissed. Huangfu Song and Zhu Jun both refused to give them anything, so Zhao Zhong and the others memorialized the throne and had them dismissed. The Emperor further appointed Zhao Zhong and others Generals of Chariots and Cavalry, while Zhang Rang and twelve others were all enfeoffed as marquises. The government grew ever more corrupt, and the people sighed and complained. Then Ou Xing, a rebel in Changsha, rose in revolt; in Yuyang, Zhang Ju and Zhang Chun rebelled: Zhang Ju proclaimed himself Son of Heaven, and Zhang Chun styled himself General-in-Chief. Urgent memorials fell like snowflakes, but the Ten Attendants concealed them all and did not report them to the throne.

p.src: One day, while the Emperor was feasting with the Ten Attendants in the rear garden, Liu Tao, Grandee Remonstrant and Consultant, came straight before him and wept aloud. The Emperor asked him why. Liu Tao said, “The realm is in peril from one dawn to the next, yet Your Majesty still drinks with these eunuchs!” The Emperor said, “The realm is at peace. What danger can there be?” Liu Tao said, “Bandits are rising on every side and plundering the provinces and commanderies. This calamity has arisen entirely because the Ten Attendants sell offices, oppress the people, and deceive their sovereign and the court. All upright men have departed from the court, and disaster stands before our very eyes!” The Ten Attendants all removed their caps and knelt prostrate before the Emperor, saying, “The great ministers will not tolerate us; we can no longer live! We beg only that our lives be spared so that we may return to our villages, and we shall devote all our household wealth to military expenses.” When they had finished, they wept bitterly. The Emperor angrily said to Liu Tao, “You too have personal attendants. Why is it only mine whom you will not tolerate?” He called for the guards to drag Liu Tao out and behead him. Liu Tao cried out, “I do not begrudge my death! But alas for the Han realm, enduring more than four hundred years, which now shall perish in a single day!”

p.src: The guards escorted Liu Tao out and were about to execute him when a high minister shouted, “Stay your hands! Wait until I have remonstrated with His Majesty.” The onlookers saw that it was Minister over the Masses Chen Dan. He went straight into the chamber and remonstrated with the Emperor: “What crime has Remonstrant Liu committed that he should be put to death?” The Emperor said, “He slandered my close attendants and affronted Our person.” Chen Dan said, “All the people under Heaven long to eat the flesh of the Ten Regular Attendants, yet Your Majesty reveres them as parents. Though they have not an inch of merit, every one of them has been enfeoffed as a marquis. Moreover, Feng Xu and the others conspired with the Yellow Turbans and sought to raise disorder within the court. If Your Majesty will not now examine your own conduct, the realm will collapse before your very eyes!” The Emperor said, “It is not proven that Feng Xu plotted rebellion. Can there not be even one or two loyal ministers among the Ten Regular Attendants?” Chen Dan struck his head against the steps as he continued his remonstrance. Enraged, the Emperor ordered him dragged away and imprisoned together with Liu Tao. That very night, the Ten Regular Attendants contrived to murder them in prison; then, forging an imperial edict, they appointed Sun Jian Administrator of Changsha and sent him to suppress Ou Xing.

p.src: Within fifty days, victory was reported and Jiangxia was pacified. An edict enfeoffed Sun Jian as Marquis of Wucheng; Liu Yu was appointed Governor of Youzhou and sent with troops to Yuyang to campaign against Zhang Ju and Zhang Chun. Liu Hui of Daizhou recommended Xuande to Liu Yu by letter. Liu Yu was delighted. He made Xuande a Commandant, and Xuande led troops straight to the rebels’ lair. After several days of fierce fighting, he blunted their ardor. Zhang Chun was wholly savage and brutal, and his soldiers’ allegiance turned. An officer under his command stabbed him to death, presented his head, and led the men in surrender. Seeing that the tide had turned against him, Zhang Ju also hanged himself. Yuyang was completely pacified. Liu Yu memorialized the throne concerning Liu Bei’s great service. The court pardoned his offense of flogging the postal inspector, appointed him Assistant Magistrate of Xiami, and then transferred him to be Commandant of Gaotang. Gongsun Zan further memorialized Xuande’s former merits, recommending him as Major of a Separate Command and acting Magistrate of Pingyuan County. At Pingyuan, Xuande acquired considerable money, grain, troops, and horses, and restored something of his former standing. For his service in suppressing the rebels, Liu Yu was appointed Grand Commandant.

p.src: In the sixth year of Zhongping, in the fourth month of summer, Emperor Ling fell gravely ill and summoned General-in-Chief He Jin to the palace to discuss the succession. He Jin had been born into a butcher’s household; but his younger sister entered the palace as an honored lady and bore the imperial son Bian. She was subsequently made Empress, and through her He Jin gained authority and high office. The Emperor also favored the Fair Lady Wang, who bore the imperial son Xie. Jealous, Empress He poisoned the Fair Lady Wang. The imperial son Xie was raised in the palace of Empress Dowager Dong. Empress Dowager Dong was Emperor Ling’s mother and the wife of Liu Chang, Marquis of Jiedu Village. Because Emperor Huan had died without a son, the son of the Marquis of Jiedu Village had been brought in and enthroned; he became Emperor Ling. After Emperor Ling inherited the imperial line, he brought his mother into the palace to support her and honored her as Empress Dowager. Empress Dowager Dong had often urged the Emperor to name the imperial son Xie Crown Prince. The Emperor, too, especially loved Xie and wished to appoint him. Now, as the Emperor lay gravely ill, Jian Shuo, a Regular Palace Attendant, memorialized: “If Your Majesty wishes to enthrone Xie, you must first execute He Jin and thereby prevent future trouble.” The Emperor approved his counsel and accordingly summoned He Jin into the palace. When He Jin reached the palace gate, the Major Pan Yin told him, “Do not enter the palace. Jian Shuo means to murder you.” Greatly alarmed, He Jin hurried back to his residence and summoned the high ministers, intending to exterminate the eunuchs. One man among those present stepped forward and said, “The power of the eunuchs began in the reigns of Emperors Chong and Zhi; their influence has spread exceedingly far throughout the court. How can they all be put to death? If the plan should leak, the calamity of exterminating your entire clan will surely follow. I beg you to consider it carefully.” He Jin looked and saw that the speaker was Cao Cao, Colonel Who Arranges the Army. He Jin rebuked him: “What can a youngster like you know of the great affairs of the court?” While he was still hesitating, Pan Yin arrived and said, “The Emperor has died. Jian Shuo and the Ten Regular Attendants are now consulting together. They are concealing the death and falsely issuing an edict to summon His Excellency the Empress’s Brother He into the palace, intending to remove future opposition and enthrone the imperial son Xie.” Before he had finished speaking, an envoy arrived, commanding He Jin to enter at once and settle the succession. Cao Cao said, “Our present course should be first to establish the rightful sovereign, and only then deal with the traitors.” He Jin said, “Who dares join me in establishing the rightful sovereign and suppressing the traitors?” One man stepped forward and said, “Lend me five thousand picked troops. I shall force the gates and enter, enthrone the new sovereign, exterminate the eunuchs, cleanse the court, and bring peace to the realm!” He Jin looked and saw the son of Minister over the Masses Yuan Feng and nephew of Yuan Wei. His name was Shao, his style Benchu, and he then held office as Colonel Director of Retainers. He Jin was overjoyed and immediately mustered five thousand imperial guards. Yuan Shao donned his full armor. He Jin led He Yong, Xun You, Zheng Tai, and more than thirty other high ministers into the palace one after another. Before Emperor Ling’s coffin, they supported Crown Prince Bian’s accession to the imperial throne.

p.src: When all the officials had finished their acclamations and obeisances, Yuan Shao entered the palace to arrest Jian Shuo. In panic, Jian Shuo fled beneath the flowering shade in the imperial garden, where Guo Sheng, a Regular Palace Attendant, killed him. All the imperial guards under Jian Shuo’s command submitted. Yuan Shao said to He Jin, “The palace eunuchs have formed a faction. Today we can seize the advantage and exterminate them.” Realizing the danger, Zhang Rang and the others hurried to report to Empress He: “The original plot to ensnare and harm the General-in-Chief was Jian Shuo’s alone; we your servants had no part in it. Now the General-in-Chief has listened to Yuan Shao and means to kill us all. We beg Your Majesty to take pity on us!” Empress Dowager He said, “Do not worry. I shall protect you.” She issued an order summoning He Jin. The Empress Dowager privately told him, “You and I were born to a humble station. Without Zhang Rang and the others, how could we ever have enjoyed such wealth and honor? Now the cruel Jian Shuo has already been executed. Why do you heed the words of others and seek to kill all the eunuchs?” After hearing her, He Jin went out and told the assembled officials, “Jian Shuo plotted to harm me, so his entire clan may be exterminated. There is no need to inflict indiscriminate slaughter upon the rest.” Yuan Shao said, “Unless you cut down the grass and tear out the roots, this will surely become the cause of your death.” He Jin said, “My mind is made up. Say no more.” All the officials withdrew.

What am I to do?” Yuan Shao said, “Summon the heroes and men of worth from every quarter, and have them lead troops to the capital to exterminate the eunuchs. With the situation made so urgent, the Empress Dowager will have no choice but to comply.” He Jin said, “An excellent plan!” He immediately issued proclamations to the various regional commands, summoning them to the capital.
